label: release-notes-cold-read
headline: Cold read of the 0.4.0 release notes as a stranger on 0.3.0: the three breaking-change facts and five of six known-open defects are correctly in the first screen, but a SIXTH open defect is absent entirely -- loaders._read_pairs drops blank-key and blank-value CSV rows from load_csv, load_long_to_short_csv and load_term_index_csv and returns a GovernedDictionary with no member saying so (reproduced: 5 data rows, 2 unusable, 3 entries, 0 warnings). Ten prose findings plus one blocker: the version bump and the whole release section are UNCOMMITTED, so the green tick D-127 records is on 6d44002, which is not the commit to tag.
shipped: A findings document only, at .github/run-summaries/mandate-iii-release-040/cold-read-release-notes-040-findings.md -- deliberately outside SCAN_GLOBS, because docs/notes/*.md is scanned and a new file of figures there would push the deferred ledger past 185 and redden the claims gate.

Eleven items: one release blocker; four HIGH (F-1 the 'two breaking changes' / 'everything else is additive' pair against three BREAKING labels; F-3 the omitted CSV-loader defect; F-7 'seven of the sixteen CLI commands' against 8 of 17; F-8 the closed self-audit series at six rounds against D-132's seven); four MEDIUM (F-2 three wrong 'first entry under X' pointers; F-9 the ninth DoD sweep shown as latest plus the stale fourteen-criteria README link; F-10 docs/GATES.md described in the present tense as 0 of 36 when it is 21 of 42; F-4 PhysicalName.unaccounted unread by the package and absent from two of three governed CLI verbs); two LOW (F-5, F-6).
Exact paste-ready replacement text for every falsehood, every figure kept inside backticks so prose_of() masks it and the deferred ledger cannot grow.

A cleared list: eleven claims verified TRUE against running code, including all 19 shim paths importing with object identity preserved, the 26-code-point round trip, the version-keyed Unicode table, both empty headline rows from tools/splits.py --check, and the three that must agree.
files_changed: .github/run-summaries/mandate-iii-release-040/cold-read-release-notes-040-findings.md (new; the only prose file this read wrote)
pre_registration: Written before reading CHANGELOG.md past its first screen. Four falsifiers. FB1 (the two breaking changes are NOT both in the first screen, so the notes fail question one) did NOT fire: both BREAKING bullets and the 19-shim paragraph are above the fold and all three verify against running code. FB2 (at least one of the five brief-named open defects is absent from the first screen) did NOT fire: all five are in the KNOWN-OPEN DEFECTS block and all five reproduce. FB3 (a sixth recorded open defect of the same class exists and is NOT in the notes) FIRED, and it is the lead finding: loaders._read_pairs, open at docs/DECISIONS.md:2636 and docs/DEFINITION-OF-DONE.md criterion 7, absent from the whole 0.4.0 section by grep. FB4 (a number in the notes is superseded by D-127..D-136) FIRED twice: the six-round 15.97 % series against D-132's seven-round 14.88 %, and the ninth DoD sweep against D-135's tenth. Magnitude prediction: 3 to 6 findings; actual 11, and the two I did not predict were structural rather than numeric -- the uncommitted version bump, and three cross-references resolving to the wrong entry.
how_it_fails: WHAT THE ADVERSARIAL PASS KILLED. My first reading of the brief's '1,076 idempotence breaks' as the notes' own figure was wrong: D-130's walk reads normalize 1,050, to_physical_name 1,076, union 1,076, disjoint True -- so the notes' 1,050 is correct for normalize and the union sentence is correct too. I nearly filed it as a falsehood; it is F-5, a clarity item, because to_physical_name's own 1,076 is never attached to a verb. I also nearly filed the 4.38 x multiple as the unqualified form docs/DECISIONS.md line 1777 records as a defect; the shipped text carries 'up to ... falling to 0.97 at the loosest' and is fixed. || HOW THIS READ FAILS: it applied nothing and mutated nothing, so 'could a gate have caught any of these?' is answered by argument rather than by method -- though F-7, F-8, F-9 and F-10 are all cross-document staleness and the claims gate is provably green over all four, because each figure is either a spelled-out word or sits inside a code span prose_of() masks. F-3's severity rests on my judgement that a CSV loader is a first-contact path for a governed user; nobody has measured how many callers use load_csv. I could not adjudicate the 3,619,227-record byte-identity claim -- third consecutive party unable to, harness uncommitted, corpora absent. I did not read the 0.3.0 and earlier sections except to locate the 28 deferred items, so a figure the 0.4.0 section contradicts further down the file would have been missed. My replacement text is untested against the claims gate because applying it was out of scope: the backtick-masking argument is derived from D-131's statement of prose_of() behaviour plus the observation that all 28 CHANGELOG deferred items sit past line 1387, not from running the gate over an edited file.
not_done: Nothing was applied. Every replacement is text for the operator; no falsehood in CHANGELOG.md is fixed on disk.
README.md lines 543, 738 and 785 carry the same stale CLI count and the same stale fourteen-criteria link. Reported, not fixed, and outside this brief.

No mutation was run on any gate, so this read adds nothing to the in-situ debt at 21 of 42.

AND THE THREE THIS SCHEMA HAS NO KEY FOR, run by this reader and all green: python tools/run_summary.py --check -> 2 rounds, 2 filed, 0 gaps rc=0; python tools/run_summary.py --check-agent-summary -> 4 directories, 3 crashes, 0 unattributable rc=0; python tools/render_figures.py --check -> 2 figures x 2 themes byte-identical, every run id resolves, rc=0. The 'gates' vocabulary here is eight names while D-127 and CONTRIBUTING.md line 88 both say ten commands must be green, so a round cannot report three of the ten in its own machine-readable account. This file is the fourth party to hit that and the first to record it inside the object itself.

claims_for_sampling: loaders.load_csv on a 5-data-row CSV with one blank-value row and one blank-key row returns a GovernedDictionary with 3 entries, emits no warning, and exposes no public member reporting the two dropped rows.
grep -ni over CHANGELOG.md lines 10 to 1298 for load_csv, _read_pairs, discards, or 'unusable row' returns no match, so the open CSV-loader defect appears nowhere in the 0.4.0 release section.
The 0.4.0 section contains three items labelled BREAKING -- at lines 18, 29 and 143 -- while its opening sentence at line 12 says 'Two breaking changes'.

acronymkit --help at this tree lists 17 commands, 8 of which read a governed vocabulary, so CHANGELOG.md line 854's 'seven of the sixteen CLI commands' is false, and the eighth governed command is governed-gap, added by this release.
docs/DECISIONS.md D-132 states the submitted-sentence series is CLOSED AT 25 of 168 = 14.88 % over SEVEN rounds, while CHANGELOG.md line 1269 publishes 15.97 % over SIX rounds as the closed figure.
tools/sample_claims.py lines 291 to 298 ship CLOSED_SERIES with rounds 6, draws 144, not_true 23, per_round (5,5,6,2,2,3).

All 19 pre-split import paths import successfully from the source tree, and acronymkit.governed.expand_identifier is acronymkit.catalog.expand_identifier evaluates True, as does the same identity test for tokenizer.
to_physical_name of U+01F0 against an empty GovernedDictionary returns physical 'J' plus U+030C with unaccounted equal to the empty tuple, and normalize on that same string raises TokenizationError.

All 28 of CHANGELOG.md's deferred-ledger items reported by python tools/check_claims.py --residue sit at lines 1387 through 1628, none of them inside the 0.4.0 section.
